Fix the following issues. The issues can be from different files or can overlap on same lines in one file.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/db.py around lines 23 - 29, The current _is_sqlite_url function's ".db" suffix check is too broad and can misidentify URLs like "postgresql://host/myapp.db" as SQLite; update _is_sqlite_url to only treat URLs as SQLite when they start with "sqlite://" or "file:" (i.e., remove the normalized.endswith(".db") check) so detection relies on explicit SQLite URL prefixes.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/db_pool.py around lines 107 - 116, The SQLite branch in the connection info function uses different hardcoded defaults for STUDIO_DB_POOL_MIN/STUDIO_DB_POOL_SIZE ("1"/"1") than the PostgreSQL branch ("2"/"5"); update the SQLite path (the block guarded by _is_sqlite_url(_load_database_url())) to use the same environment variable defaults as the other backend (STUDIO_DB_POOL_MIN default 2 and STUDIO_DB_POOL_SIZE default 5) or centralize those defaults into a single constant used by both branches so both _is_sqlite_url and the PostgreSQL code read the same fallback values for pool_min and pool_max.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/db_pool.py around lines 60 - 66, The current _get_sqlite_pool_connection returns a single global _sqlite_pool_conn which is unsafe for concurrent threads; change it to provide a thread-local connection instead: introduce a threading.local (e.g. _sqlite_conn_tls) and have _get_sqlite_pool_connection check/create a per-thread attribute (using get_sqlite_connection and _load_database_url) so each thread gets its own SQLiteConnection, or alternatively create a new connection per-call; ensure you remove reliance on the global _sqlite_pool_conn and document lifecycle/close semantics for the per-thread connections.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/db_sqlite.py at line 124, The naive .replace("%s", "?") on adapted_sql can alter '%s' inside string literals; update the conversion so placeholders are only replaced when outside single-quoted strings by replacing the single-line replace with a small helper used after pg_to_sqlite(sql) (e.g., replace_placeholders_outside_quotes or sanitize_placeholders) that scans the SQL or uses a regex like alternating quoted-string vs placeholder pattern to only swap real parameter tokens to '?' and leaves quoted '%s' intact; apply this helper where adapted_sql is set so pg_to_sqlite(sql) output is safely converted.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/db_sqlite.py around lines 46 - 56, The current datetime parsing block that checks value[10] and tries formats ("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f", "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S", "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f") misses ISO8601 timezone suffixes like "Z" or "+01:00" and can return the original string for those cases; update the parsing logic for the same value variable to first normalize timezone tokens (e.g., convert a trailing "Z" to "+00:00" and normalize offsets) and then attempt parsing with datetime.fromisoformat or include formats with %z (e.g., "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z" and "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.%f%z"), falling back to the existing formats only if timezone-aware parsing fails so timezone-containing ISO8601 strings produce proper datetime objects.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/db_sqlite.py around lines 63 - 66, The bool branch is unreachable because bool is a subclass of int and the isinstance(value, (str, int, float, bytes)) check runs first; move the bool check to precede the int/float check so booleans are converted to ints (e.g., return int(value)) before generic numeric/string handling; update the type-conversion block that inspects value (the isinstance calls) accordingly and run/adjust any tests that rely on boolean storage behavior.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/migrations/versions/001_initial_schema.py around lines 418 - 422, Duplicate UUID SQL is defined as SQLITE_UUID_DEFAULT in this migration but the canonical string lives as _UUID_SQL in shared/sql_dialect.py; remove the duplicated literal from shared/migrations/versions/001_initial_schema.py and import or reference the single source of truth (use _UUID_SQL from shared/sql_dialect.py or re-export it) so both the migration and application code share the same UUID SQL symbol and avoid drift.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/repository.py around lines 438 - 443, The code interpolates table_name directly into the PRAGMA SQL (PRAGMA table_info({table_name})) creating SQL injection risk; to fix this, validate table_name before use by ensuring it is a legal identifier (e.g. match regex r'^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$' or check against an explicit whitelist) and raise an exception if it fails validation, then use the validated value in the PRAGMA call (keep the existing PRAGMA table_info({table_name}) call but only after validation). Reference the table_name variable and the PRAGMA table_info(...) call in this block so the validation sits immediately before executing cur.execute(...).

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @shared/sql_dialect.py at line 76, The current global replacement out = re.sub(r"\s+CASCADE\b", "", out, flags=re.IGNORECASE) removes CASCADE everywhere; change it to only strip CASCADE following DROP TABLE or DROP VIEW. Update the substitution to target CASCADE when it's part of a DROP TABLE/VIEW clause (e.g. match patterns like \bDROP\s+(?:TABLE|VIEW)[^;]*\s+CASCADE\b) and remove the CASCADE token only within that matched group (use a regex with a callback or a two-step regex that locates DROP TABLE/VIEW blocks and strips their trailing CASCADE), modifying the same variable out. Ensure the replacement preserves other occurrences such as ON DELETE CASCADE.

- Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In @tests/conftest.py around lines 25 - 31, The helper function _is_sqlite_url in tests/conftest.py is a duplicate of the one in shared/db.py; remove the local definition and import the single canonical function from shared.db instead (e.g. from shared.db import _is_sqlite_url), update any local references to use the imported symbol, and run tests to ensure the import path is correct and there are no circular import issues.
